items.method: Cross-read the market-heatmap breadth percentage against its 60% threshold and against the benchmark's distance from its 52-week high and its MA stack, then overlay the option-flow call fraction and put-versus-call premium and the VIX band to judge whether an index holding near highs is being carried by a narrowing set of leaders.
items.note: A narrow-leadership divergence has opened into this pre-market window. SPY's benchmark sits at 776.34, just 0.2% under its 52-week high in a bull-stacked MA regime (50-day distance +3.71%, 200-day +10.47%, 126-day momentum +14.56%), yet only 26.1% of the 134 market-heatmap constituents are positive on the day — a 33.9-point shortfall to the 60% broad-participation threshold. At the same time option flow has leaned put-heavy: calls are just 37.2% of premium, with about $1.30B of call premium against $2.21B of puts across 12 tickers and 1675 flagged contracts. VIX 15.87 keeps this in the pressure-not-panic band, and swing structure still reads bull-stacked with an active double bottom over 517 bars. A headline index pinned near its high on 26% breadth while hedging demand rises is the classic thinning-leadership pattern, where the average stock is already rolling over beneath a firm index. This is what to watch: whether breadth re-broadens back toward the threshold or the index converges down to a weakening tape.
items.title: Index holds within 0.2% of its 52-week high while daily breadth collapses to 26% and option flow turns put-heavy

inputs: options-structure-lab.regime=negative; signedNetGEX=-4.83B; flip=774.77; callWall=773; putWall=768; expectedMove=10.65; spot=769.1
intraday-tape-lab.sessionType=Trend day down; control=Mixed; vwap=774.1; gapPct=-0.02
items.method: Read the options-structure signed net-gamma sign with its flip and wall levels against current spot, size the expected-move band, confirm the dealer scenario and hold from the gamma playbook, then overlay the most-unusual option prints and the prior-session intraday VWAP to judge whether short-gamma dealers are positioned to accelerate a break of the nearest wall.
items.note: Dealer positioning and price have converged on the lower edge of the gamma structure this window. Signed net gamma is negative at about -$4.83B, and SPY spot 769.1 has dropped below the 774.77 flip to sit just above the 768 put wall with the 773 call wall overhead. The front expected move has widened to plus or minus 10.65 — a far looser band than a tightly pinned structure — so the 768-to-773 wall corridor no longer confines price the way a compressed band would. Under negative gamma dealers hedge in the direction of the move, so pressure at a wall tends to extend rather than mean-revert. The flow tape agrees: the single most unusual print in the feed is a same-day SPY 775 put at $209.1M on 75.9x open interest, the largest premium on the board, and overall flow is put-heavy. The prior live auction was a trend-day-down under mixed control with VWAP 774.1 above spot. This is a coiled range-break-watch structure with a patient, same-session-fade playbook: while 768 holds and VIX 15.87 stays calm it can stay orderly, but a sustained loss of the 768 put wall in short-gamma is the level that would tip the balance toward downside acceleration rather than a fade.
items.title: SPY prints below the negative-gamma flip and rests just above the 768 put wall as the expected-move band widens to plus or minus 10.65
